pairs.question: In quot primas partes legis diuinae scientia diuiditur?
pairs.answer: In duas, quarum una ad ipsam superficiem dictionis proprie pertinet, alia in rebus est quas ipsa scriptura nos edocet.
pairs.derivation: Catechetical master/disciple dialogue. Stripped the [Delta] (master) and [Mu] (disciple) speaker labels. Question is a real interrogative; answer is the disciple's complete self-contained reply (single sentence to the full stop).

pairs.question: Species dictionis quot sunt?
pairs.answer: Quattuor: nam aut historica est aut prophetica aut prouerbialis aut simpliciter docens.
pairs.derivation: Stripped the leading section number '2.' and the [Delta]/[Mu] speaker labels. Interrogative question; answer enumerates the four kinds, complete to the full stop.

pairs.question: Historia quid est?
pairs.derivation: Stripped the [Delta]/[Mu] speaker labels. Real interrogative definition-question; the disciple's whole answer is this single definitional phrase.

pairs.question: Quid est prophetia?
pairs.answer: Rerum latentium praeteritarum aut praesentium aut futurarum ex diuina inspiratione manifestatio.
pairs.derivation: Stripped the [Delta]/[Mu] speaker labels. Interrogative definition-question answered by the disciple's complete defining sentence.

pairs.question: Quae est prouerbialis species?
pairs.answer: Quaedam figurata locutio, aliud sonans, aliud sentiens, et in praesenti commonens tempore.
pairs.derivation: Stripped the [Delta]/[Mu] speaker labels. Interrogative question, complete self-contained answer to the full stop.

pairs.question: Quae est simplex doctrina?
pairs.answer: Qua de fide aut de moribus in praesenti tempore simpliciter edocemur.
pairs.derivation: Stripped the [Delta]/[Mu] speaker labels. Interrogative definition-question; the disciple's full reply answers it directly.

pairs.question: Quid est uoluntas?
pairs.answer: Vis animi inuiolata siue spontanea, secundum quam diuersae atque contrariae cogitationes efficiuntur et opera.
pairs.derivation: Stripped the [Delta]/[Mu] speaker labels and the master's non-questioning transitional preamble 'Quoniam satis dictum est de accidentibus naturarum, dicendum nunc de accidentibus uoluntati.', advancing the question to the operative interrogative 'Quid est uoluntas?'. Answer is the disciple's complete defining sentence; stopped before the following question 'Naturalis est in nobis...'.

pairs.question: Quam uocamus acceptionem, siue uocationem?
pairs.answer: Eam scilicet qua Deus quosdam homines uel populos specialis gratiae beneficio sibi conciliare dignatur, plusque circa eos quam circa ceteros homines diuinae indulgentiae et quasi familiares fauores ostendit.
pairs.derivation: Stripped the [Delta]/[Mu] speaker labels. Interrogative definition-question; the disciple's whole self-contained reply answers it, to the full stop.

pairs.question: Quid est ergo typus, siue figura?
pairs.answer: Praesentium aut praeteritarum aut futurarum rerum ignotarum per opera, secundum id quod opera sunt, manifestatio.
pairs.derivation: Stripped the [Delta]/[Mu] speaker labels. Used the second, operative definition-question (the prior 'Quid est typus?' is answered only by a meta-remark naming the term, not a definition). This interrogative is answered by the disciple's complete defining sentence.

pairs.question: Quid est praedictio?
pairs.answer: Futurarum incertarum rerum uerbis, in quantum uerba sunt, manifestatio.
pairs.derivation: Stripped the [Delta]/[Mu] speaker labels and the master's non-questioning preamble 'Quoniam typorum regulam diximus, de praedictionibus uideamus.', advancing to the interrogative 'Quid est praedictio?'. Answer is the disciple's complete defining sentence.

pairs.question: Quid sunt igitur effectus?
pairs.answer: Effectus sunt exitus rerum, quas aut acceptionum prospiciebat intentio aut typorum similitudo figurabat aut praedictionum scientia praeloquebatur.
pairs.derivation: Stripped the [Delta]/[Mu] speaker labels and the master's non-questioning transitional preamble 'Quoniam tres iam partes ostendimus eorum quae ad futurum saeculum diximus pertinere, hoc est acceptiones et figuras et praedictiones, nunc quarta pars restat, ut de effectibus disseramus.', advancing to the interrogative 'Quid sunt igitur effectus?'. Answer is the disciple's complete defining sentence.
